Rename Proofline agent skill to proofline-check

## Why
Intentline's existing skills use the `<project>-<action>` convention (`intentline-plan`, `intentline-audit`, `intentline-slice`), while Proofline's single skill currently declares `name: proofline` in its root `SKILL.md`. Renaming that skill to **`proofline-check`** makes its purpose clearer and makes explicit invocation consistent across the two projects.

## Scope
Rename **the skill**, not the Proofline project, Python package, or CLI. Keep **one** Proofline skill covering check-only verification, evidence/feedback, optional Intentline input, and optional managed `run`. Prioritize agent-friendly discoverability, correct installation guidance, and minimal change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Change the canonical skill's frontmatter to `name: proofline-check` with a concise trigger-focused description: use after an existing coding agent implements a change to execute selected tests against the frozen candidate and report actual failures / missing evidence; mention that it is optional and model-free in `check` mode.
- [ ] Determine and document the supported skill installation/discovery path for at least Codex and Claude Code. If a standard `skills/proofline-check/SKILL.md` directory is needed, provide it without silently breaking the existing root `SKILL.md` entry or creating two independently maintained divergent instructions. Preserve relative documentation/code links under the chosen layout.
- [ ] Update README, skill instructions, examples, and any current references that invoke or install the skill under its old name. Distinguish **automatic discovery when installed** from guaranteed automatic invocation (not guaranteed).
- [ ] Preserve the existing `proofline.py check`, `run`, and `status` commands, direct/file source inputs, optional Intentline integration, zero-extra-model check-only behavior, receipt integrity, and safety boundaries. Do **not** rename the CLI to `proofline-check`.
- [ ] Test/validate skill metadata, single canonical definition or explicit compatibility alias (if needed), relative link resolution, supported install packaging, and documentation consistency. If an old explicit skill invocation is no longer supported, document the migration clearly rather than claiming unverified compatibility.
- [ ] Confirm no new mandatory planning, reviewer/prover, authorization, or model-dispatch stage was introduced.

## Out of scope
Splitting Proofline into multiple skills merely for symmetry, changing Intentline skill names, merging repositories, altering check execution semantics, or making skill discovery mandatory for direct CLI use.

---
name: proofline
description: Model-free checks on an existing frozen working candidate, or one optional coding attempt, without universal correctness certification.
---

Use the [supported local runner](proofline.py) `check` command for existing
agent work: **zero model dispatches**, **macOS**, Python 3.11+ and **Codex CLI
0.162.1** (sandbox only; no model authentication needed). The optional `run`
command needs authentication and a clean Git source for one coding attempt.
Only `run --correct-once` opts in to one follow-up correction on that same
native implementer thread; successful first passes never dispatch another turn.
Historical `deliver` and `resume` are unsupported. Direct requests need no
P2P/Intentline workflow.

Use the simplest form first: preserve the user's **entire original
request** in `--request` (verbatim text) or `--request-stdin` (exact UTF-8
bytes including terminal newlines) and provide one explicit project-native
`--command` per relevant check. Neither a saved request file nor
`checks.json` is required. For durable/complex inputs, the original
`--source FILE` and `--checks FILE` interfaces still work unchanged.
Each `--command` is POSIX-quoted **argv**, not a shell invocation; no
expansion, glob, pipe or command substitution runs. Provide an absolute
executable path and quote arguments accurately; use `--checks` JSON for
difficult argv. Source and check input forms are each mutually exclusive.

Do not fabricate expected results, silently narrow requested behavior,
or modify unrelated user work. `check` copies current tracked bytes plus non-ignored
untracked files, preserves regular file modes and safe relative file symlinks,
and omits tracked deletions. Pause edits during capture; changes detected across
two reads invalidate the snapshot. Ignored untracked files, Git metadata and
empty directories are excluded. Submodules, nested repositories, directory or
escaping symlinks, FIFOs, sockets and devices have no supported observation path.
There is no unprotected fallback on unsupported files or platforms. The source
repository stays untouched, including its index, dirty and untracked work.

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B /absolute/path/to/proofline/proofline.py check \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/product \
  --request 'Reject whitespace-only usernames; preserve Unicode and CLI behavior.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests'
```

No new model is dispatched for this existing-agent check. For a managed one-agent
attempt on a **clean** source repository, `run` accepts the same direct inputs:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B /absolute/path/to/proofline/proofline.py run \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/clean-product \
  --request 'Add --version while preserving CLI output.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests' \
  --stage-seconds 600
```

For multiline source from a command-capable host, use `--request-stdin`
with a pipe that preserves exact UTF-8 bytes; avoid trimming or summarizing
the request.

The output must be a new directory outside the source repository (default:
system temporary directory, `proofline-check/<unique-id>`). Preserve it for
later evidence readback. `check` never resets, stashes or commits in the source;
only its isolated copy receives a Git identity. For managed coding, use `run`
with the same arguments and `--stage-seconds 600` on a clean source.

The coding agent owns strategy, self-checks and repairs. Proofline runs the
caller-selected commands against its frozen, read-only candidate under native
protection. The source, selected files, command arrays and separate host receipts
are bound to the report. All time counts toward the episode budget. No network
access, dependency installation, AI reviewer/prover, publication,
merge or deployment runs. Linux offline CI does not establish a native macOS
qualification. Existing authorization rules still apply; local checking never
permits external mutations.

**Optional managed correction (#15):** Add `--correct-once` only to `run`.
Require a failed selected executable check with intact bound native evidence
and a Python `AssertionError` diagnostic. Every selected check must be
available; environment errors, arbitrary nonzero exits, timeouts, truncated
logs, stale inputs, caller annotations and advisory promise/Intentline gaps
cannot trigger a turn. Unsupported failure formats remain for the caller.
Proofline resumes the bound original implementer once with the unchanged
full source and exact native observations, copies and freezes a new candidate,
then reruns all selected checks. One `--seconds` budget covers the whole
episode; neither correction nor interruption resets it. The initial report
is retained at `initial/report.json` and checked again by `status`.
Dispatch slots are reserved before launch and an uncertain interrupted slot
cannot be reused. Controller resume is unsupported; never silently start a
new episode. A repeated defect stops with its actual failed/unavailable status,
not another correction or automatic acceptance certification. `check`
continues to dispatch zero models and leaves corrections to the existing agent.

For failed checks, read the bounded CLI **Feedback** summary first; consult
`report.json` -> `feedback.checks` for exact argv, exit status, elapsed
time, candidate/source identity, and `receipts/check-NNN.json` for the native
bounded stdout/stderr. Treat timeouts, missing executables, truncated logs,
sandbox failure and stale evidence as **unavailable**, not implementation
failures. Do not invent a failure's expected/observed behavior.

When the caller already knows a specific expected/observed case, optionally
attach `--failure-details /private/failure-details.json` containing rows
`{"index":0,"outcome_ids":["R2"],"expected":"accepted","observed":"rejected"}`.
The observed text must be present in the host-captured failed-check output;
otherwise it is **not** reported as observed. Expected text and R IDs remain
unverified caller claims; the optional #13 source mapping can validate ID and
command associations, not semantic completeness. No new
AI invocation, workflow, or mandatory metadata file is needed.

**Optional promise mapping (no extra model):** When the same agent or
caller already has a few source-grounded outcomes, provide
`--promises /private/promises.json` only to `check`. The file is a small
JSON object with `schema_version: 1`, `source_sha256` of the **entire
exact original UTF-8 request**, and `requirements` containing unique `R1`,
`R2` ... entries. Each row needs a short `statement`, a `source_refs` list
of `{"source_id":"S1","line_start":1,"line_end":1,"quote":"exact original line"}`,
and `checks` entries of `{"index":0,"argv":[...]}` matching *exactly* the
selected check at that zero-based index; empty `checks` is allowed and means
**NOT DEMONSTRATED**. Optional `kind` is outcome/constraint/exception and
`oracle` is only a **proposed expectation**, never executable proof.
An optional `candidate_tree` pins one specific frozen Git tree; mismatches
fail before native checks. Keep the original source unchanged and never
represent an omitted source clause as approved scope.

To look for overlooked user promises **without another agent**, optionally
reread the *entire original source* and supplied rows/checks once, then add
`review: {"performed":true,"proposals":[...]}`. Each advisory proposal
needs a source-quoted `statement` and `suggested_check` (text only,
never executed). Do not fabricate source quotes, confidence or authority.
If no review occurred, omit it: the default is `performed:false`.
Even if the reviewer found zero gaps, completeness remains **UNKNOWN**.
The new `promise_evidence` report records linked passes (limited evidence),
actual failures, unavailable checks and unlinked/not demonstrated R rows,
plus proposal provenance. Source identity, exact check argv, frozen candidate,
mapping and receipts are checked again by `status`. To display **all** original
request text, call `proofline.py status RECORD --show-source`.
For the exact JSON shape and a concrete example, see [README](README.md).
No Intentline, planning stage, approval, or second AI model is required.

Use `proofline.py status <report.json>` to revalidate the frozen inputs and receipts.
New live-source edits require a new `check`; an old record refers to its old snapshot.
Report the exact candidate, actual named check results and uncovered
requirements. `CHECKS PASSED` means only that listed commands exited
successfully. Distinguish `CHECKS FAILED`, `CHECKS UNAVAILABLE`,
`EXECUTION UNAVAILABLE`, and `STALE CHECKS`. Never call checks
full-promise certification or claim a PR/merge occurred.

**Optional Intentline guidance:** For complex requests, this same existing
agent may use [Intentline's plan skill](https://github.com/grove/intentline/blob/main/skills/intentline-plan/SKILL.md)
to identify proposed `R` outcomes, edge cases, and candidate checks, then call
Proofline `check` against the unchanged original request and chosen argv.
That plan is advisory, not proven behavior or permission.
**No Intentline installation, contract adoption, extra approval, or model
stage is required by Proofline**.

For an already-prepared **single original-request Intentline JSON export**,
optionally pass `--intentline-export /private/json-export` to `check`
and `--source /private/json-export/source-S1.txt`. The existing agent still
selects real commands, and can optionally provide `--intentline-links
/private/links.json`, e.g. `{"R1":[{"index":0,"argv":["/absolute/python",
"-m","unittest"]}]}` matching the selected check argv **exactly**. If
links are absent, every imported R is NOT DEMONSTRATED; planning notes
alone never execute or certify a test. `--intentline-export` and
`--promises` are mutually exclusive. Unsupported S2 contexts, amendments,
native bundles or partial/symlinked exports are refused without fallback.
See [README](README.md) and [#23](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/23).

Preserve Intentline's proposed oracles, boundaries, evidence gaps, constraints
and exclusions **as advisory data**; do not treat `unapproved` or
`operator_asserted_unverified` markers as authenticated consent, independent
acceptance or permission to publish. Never run exported scripts. No Intentline
Python package is imported by the adapter; ordinary check-only runs work
without it.

The [vNext contract](DESIGN.md) and [open issues](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues)
retain zero-extra-model check-only use and prioritize useful failure feedback.
New mandatory stages must demonstrate improvements in independently
correct deliveries that justify their latency, cost and blocking risk.
# Proofline

**A small, optional helper to autonomous coding agents.** Proofline preserves
an original request, freezes an existing working candidate, and executes
caller-selected checks without another model dispatch. It also offers one
optional bounded coding attempt. Passing commands are evidence
**only about those commands**, not proof of every requirement.

## Quick start — let the existing agent check its work

No planning step, acceptance-contract file, or test-configuration file is needed.
After implementing a change, the **same coding agent** chooses relevant,
already-available project checks and calls Proofline directly:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py check \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/product \
  --request 'Reject blank usernames while preserving Unicode and CLI compatibility.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B cli.py --version'
```

This is an example: choose commands and public interfaces that actually exist
in the target repository. `check` captures the working tree (including ordinary
uncommitted changes), runs exactly those checks and **dispatches zero coding
models**. Its returned report names the frozen candidate and any failed or
unavailable checks, not an automatic assertion that every request was fulfilled.

For a bounded **optional managed coding attempt**, use the same direct inputs:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py run \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/clean-product \
  --request 'Add a --version flag without changing existing CLI behavior.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests' \
  --stage-seconds 600
```

`run` requires an authenticated Codex CLI and a clean Git source, and launches
one coding attempt. It does **not** add an AI reviewer, prover, planner or PR
publisher. No extra model is launched by `check`.

For one optional correction by that **same implementer**, add `--correct-once`
to `run`. First-pass success still uses just one dispatch. Only an intact,
nonzero native check with a Python `AssertionError` diagnostic qualifies;
every selected check must have usable evidence. Timeouts, missing tools,
truncated or mismatched receipts, stale candidates, environment-error
diagnostics, advisory requirements and untested promises never trigger it.
Other failure formats are reported for the caller to handle; Proofline does
not infer a product defect from an arbitrary nonzero exit.

The correction resumes the original native thread with the **entire original
request**, exact failed argv, exit codes and bounded stdout/stderr. It edits
a separate copy of the failed candidate, freezes it, and reruns **all** selected
checks, including compatibility checks that previously passed. `--seconds`
is one cumulative episode budget for setup, coding, checks, correction and
rerun; `--stage-seconds` caps each coding turn within that budget. There is
at most one correction, even if the defect repeats or the handoff is incomplete.
No reviewer, prover, supervisor, Intentline dependency or acceptance verdict
is introduced.

`report.json` records `correction.enabled`, `correction.attempted`, bound worker
thread and dispatch count. Dispatch slots are journaled before launch; an
interrupted launch conservatively consumes its slot. Initial candidate/check
evidence remains at `initial/report.json`, hash-bound to the final report.
Old passing checks never carry forward to an altered candidate. `status`
revalidates both candidates, source, commands and receipts; drift makes the
final evidence stale. Interrupted episodes remain unavailable and cannot
reuse their output directory. There is **no controller resume or automatic
restart** to reset the budget or repeat a dispatch; a new explicitly requested
episode uses a new output directory.

The opt-in [native control](tests/test_correction_live.py) deliberately retains
a seeded assertion defect on its first handoff, then tests same-thread
correction, native boundaries and rerun. It is a mechanism qualification,
not a measurement of improvement on ordinary coding tasks.
The [13 October 2026 qualification summary](docs/ISSUE15-QUALIFICATION.json)
records both native boundaries, the failed assertion, same-thread identities,
corrected check results and exact runtime hashes; raw evidence remains at its
recorded local path. Reproduce it on the supported authenticated host with:

```sh
PROOFLINE_CORRECTION_LIVE=1 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest tests.test_correction_live -v
```

`--request` is a single **literal** argument: multiline text and terminal
newlines are preserved if the calling host passes them. For an exact multiline
request without shell quoting, use `--request-stdin` and pipe the original
UTF-8 bytes into standard input instead. `--source FILE` remains supported
for saved original request bytes. These three sources are mutually exclusive.

Repeat `--command` for each executable check. Each value is tokenized with
POSIX quoting into one **argv array**, without executing a shell, expanding
environment variables, interpreting pipes or performing command substitutions.
Every executable must have an **absolute path**. For exact complex argv
(e.g. literal spaces, shell metacharacters or arbitrary arguments), keep using
the existing `--checks FILE` JSON format. The two check-input forms are
mutually exclusive. No extra config or dependency installation is performed.

**Optional Intentline-guided workflow (not an integration requirement):**
The existing agent may first use
[Intentline's planning skill](https://github.com/grove/intentline/blob/main/skills/intentline-plan/SKILL.md)
to identify source-grounded `R` requirements and important checks, then use
the ordinary Proofline `check` command above against the **original request**.
That advice is not an independent test result, approval, or replacement for
original source bytes. If a **completed Intentline JSON export** already exists,
Proofline can consume it optionally using `--intentline-export` (see below).
The CLI never installs or imports Intentline.

## Actionable, receipt-grounded feedback

Both `check` (zero model calls) and optional managed `run` print a **short**
summary of the selected commands. Failing commands show their exact argv
(in the structured report), native exit status, elapsed time, and a bounded
stderr/stdout excerpt with a concrete next action. An unavailable sandbox,
timeout, truncated output, stale evidence or missing executable is **not**
reported as a product defect. Successful commands give one short summary,
not another AI reviewer pass.

`report.json` includes `feedback.checks` with the exact selected argv,
exit code, elapsed seconds, frozen source SHA-256, candidate commit/tree,
snapshot identity and `receipts/check-NNN.json#stdout` / `#stderr` references.
The native host receipts are also retained as separate bounded/redacted files
**outside the command-writable scratch and the candidate**. `status` validates
their hashes and the frozen inputs; changed or missing evidence becomes
`STALE CHECKS`. Full bounded receipts are available on disk; the terminal
does not dump them by default.

If a checker already provides a specific failure example, a caller can attach
**optional** `--failure-details /private/failure-details.json`:

```json
[
  {
    "index": 0,
    "outcome_ids": ["R2"],
    "expected": "Unicode username accepted",
    "observed": "Unicode rejected"
  }
]
```

Indexes are zero-based and correspond to the selected commands. The
`expected` field is **caller-supplied, not an independently established
oracle**; the `observed` text is displayed only if it literally occurs in
the bounded native stdout/stderr of a failed check. An unsupported or forged
observation is withheld rather than presented as fact. An `R2` label without
an optional `--promises` mapping remains unverified advice; with a mapping,
its exact command association is validated but a green check still does not
prove the requirement in full. No unlisted requirement is deemed covered,
and no failed or missing evidence triggers an AI correction without the
explicit managed `run --correct-once` option and qualifying native diagnostics.

This file is optional. Ordinary `--command` or `--checks` invocations
still work unchanged, without Intentline, an acceptance plan, or extra
model dispatches. Live macOS/Codex sandbox qualification is distinct from
offline CI.

## Optional source-linked promise evidence

Existing `check` works exactly as before with **no planning or metadata**.
For a complex request, the same existing coding agent can *optionally* reread
the **full original request**, write a small source-linked JSON mapping,
and pass `--promises /private/promises.json` to `proofline.py check`.
Proofline does **not** extract requirements or generate tests on its own.
A user can also author the file directly.

For example, if `request.md` contains **exactly** these two lines:

```text
Reject blank usernames.
Support Unicode usernames.
```

An advisory mapping can be:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "source_sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_SHA256_OF_EXACT_UTF8_REQUEST_BYTES",
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "R1",
      "statement": "Reject blank usernames",
      "source_refs": [{"source_id":"S1","line_start":1,"line_end":1,
                       "quote":"Reject blank usernames."}],
      "checks": [{"index":0,"argv":["/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14","-B",
                                  "-m","unittest","discover","-s","tests"]}]
    },
    {
      "id": "R2",
      "statement": "Accept valid Unicode usernames",
      "source_refs": [{"source_id":"S1","line_start":2,"line_end":2,
                       "quote":"Support Unicode usernames."}],
      "oracle": "A valid José username should be accepted (unverified suggestion)",
      "checks": []
    }
  ]
}
```

Compute the SHA-256 from the *exact* original request file bytes
(`python3 -c 'import hashlib,sys;print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' request.md`)
and replace the placeholder. `--source /absolute/path/request.md` must refer
to the same bytes. A referenced check has a **zero-based** index and its
**exact selected argv array**; the example command must actually be among the
`--command` or `--checks` arguments. An unlinked requirement (`checks: []`)

# Proofline

**A small, optional helper to autonomous coding agents.** Proofline preserves
an original request, freezes an existing working candidate, and executes
caller-selected checks without another model dispatch. It also offers one
optional bounded coding attempt. Passing commands are evidence
**only about those commands**, not proof of every requirement.

## Quick start — let the existing agent check its work

No planning step, acceptance-contract file, or test-configuration file is needed.
After implementing a change, the **same coding agent** chooses relevant,
already-available project checks and calls Proofline directly:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py check \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/product \
  --request 'Reject blank usernames while preserving Unicode and CLI compatibility.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B cli.py --version'
```

This is an example: choose commands and public interfaces that actually exist
in the target repository. `check` captures the working tree (including ordinary
uncommitted changes), runs exactly those checks and **dispatches zero coding
models**. Its returned report names the frozen candidate and any failed or
unavailable checks, not an automatic assertion that every request was fulfilled.

For a bounded **optional managed coding attempt**, use the same direct inputs:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py run \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/clean-product \
  --request 'Add a --version flag without changing existing CLI behavior.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests' \
  --stage-seconds 600
```

`run` requires an authenticated Codex CLI and a clean Git source, and launches
one coding attempt. It does **not** add an AI reviewer, prover, planner or PR
publisher. No extra model is launched by `check`.

For one optional correction by that **same implementer**, add `--correct-once`
to `run`. First-pass success still uses just one dispatch. Only an intact,
nonzero native check with a Python `AssertionError` diagnostic qualifies;
every selected check must have usable evidence. Timeouts, missing tools,
truncated or mismatched receipts, stale candidates, environment-error
diagnostics, advisory requirements and untested promises never trigger it.
Other failure formats are reported for the caller to handle; Proofline does
not infer a product defect from an arbitrary nonzero exit.

The correction resumes the original native thread with the **entire original
request**, exact failed argv, exit codes and bounded stdout/stderr. It edits
a separate copy of the failed candidate, freezes it, and reruns **all** selected
checks, including compatibility checks that previously passed. `--seconds`
is one cumulative episode budget for setup, coding, checks, correction and
rerun; `--stage-seconds` caps each coding turn within that budget. There is
at most one correction, even if the defect repeats or the handoff is incomplete.
No reviewer, prover, supervisor, Intentline dependency or acceptance verdict
is introduced.

`report.json` records `correction.enabled`, `correction.attempted`, bound worker
thread and dispatch count. Dispatch slots are journaled before launch; an
interrupted launch conservatively consumes its slot. Initial candidate/check
evidence remains at `initial/report.json`, hash-bound to the final report.
Old passing checks never carry forward to an altered candidate. `status`
revalidates both candidates, source, commands and receipts; drift makes the
final evidence stale. Interrupted episodes remain unavailable and cannot
reuse their output directory. There is **no controller resume or automatic
restart** to reset the budget or repeat a dispatch; a new explicitly requested
episode uses a new output directory.

The opt-in [native control](tests/test_correction_live.py) deliberately retains
a seeded assertion defect on its first handoff, then tests same-thread
correction, native boundaries and rerun. It is a mechanism qualification,
not a measurement of improvement on ordinary coding tasks.
The [13 October 2026 qualification summary](docs/ISSUE15-QUALIFICATION.json)
records both native boundaries, the failed assertion, same-thread identities,
corrected check results and exact runtime hashes; raw evidence remains at its
recorded local path. Reproduce it on the supported authenticated host with:

```sh
PROOFLINE_CORRECTION_LIVE=1 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest tests.test_correction_live -v
```

`--request` is a single **literal** argument: multiline text and terminal
newlines are preserved if the calling host passes them. For an exact multiline
request without shell quoting, use `--request-stdin` and pipe the original
UTF-8 bytes into standard input instead. `--source FILE` remains supported
for saved original request bytes. These three sources are mutually exclusive.

Repeat `--command` for each executable check. Each value is tokenized with
POSIX quoting into one **argv array**, without executing a shell, expanding
environment variables, interpreting pipes or performing command substitutions.
Every executable must have an **absolute path**. For exact complex argv
(e.g. literal spaces, shell metacharacters or arbitrary arguments), keep using
the existing `--checks FILE` JSON format. The two check-input forms are
mutually exclusive. No extra config or dependency installation is performed.

**Optional Intentline-guided workflow (not an integration requirement):**
The existing agent may first use
[Intentline's planning skill](https://github.com/grove/intentline/blob/main/skills/intentline-plan/SKILL.md)
to identify source-grounded `R` requirements and important checks, then use
the ordinary Proofline `check` command above against the **original request**.
That advice is not an independent test result, approval, or replacement for
original source bytes. If a **completed Intentline JSON export** already exists,
Proofline can consume it optionally using `--intentline-export` (see below).
The CLI never installs or imports Intentline.

## Actionable, receipt-grounded feedback

Both `check` (zero model calls) and optional managed `run` print a **short**
summary of the selected commands. Failing commands show their exact argv
(in the structured report), native exit status, elapsed time, and a bounded
stderr/stdout excerpt with a concrete next action. An unavailable sandbox,
timeout, truncated output, stale evidence or missing executable is **not**
reported as a product defect. Successful commands give one short summary,
not another AI reviewer pass.

`report.json` includes `feedback.checks` with the exact selected argv,
exit code, elapsed seconds, frozen source SHA-256, candidate commit/tree,
snapshot identity and `receipts/check-NNN.json#stdout` / `#stderr` references.
The native host receipts are also retained as separate bounded/redacted files
**outside the command-writable scratch and the candidate**. `status` validates
their hashes and the frozen inputs; changed or missing evidence becomes
`STALE CHECKS`. Full bounded receipts are available on disk; the terminal
does not dump them by default.

If a checker already provides a specific failure example, a caller can attach
**optional** `--failure-details /private/failure-details.json`:
interface remains supported: save the exact UTF-8 original request in `source.md`
outside product changes and selected argv arrays in `checks.json`:

```json
[["/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14", "-B", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"]]
```

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py check \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/product \
  --source /absolute/path/to/source.md \
  --checks /absolute/path/to/checks.json \
  --output /absolute/path/outside/product/check-record \
  --seconds 900 --check-seconds 120
```

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py status /absolute/path/to/report.json
```

`check` selects **current working bytes** of tracked files (including staged
and unstaged work) plus non-ignored untracked files. Deleted tracked files are
omitted; ignored untracked files, Git metadata and empty directories are not
copied. Tracked files remain included even if an ignore rule matches them.
Regular file bytes and modes, and safe relative symlinks to files inside the
snapshot, are preserved. Submodules, nested repositories, directory or escaping
symlinks, FIFOs, sockets and devices are unsupported and rejected when selected;
ignored untracked files remain excluded. Linux and Windows have no supported
execution boundary. There is **no unprotected fallback**.

Pause edits while the candidate is copied; two reads detect changes during
capture and refuse a mixed snapshot. `check` never resets, stashes, commits in,
or writes to the source. Its isolated copy gets its own local Git identity.
The output directory must be new and outside the source repository; by default
it is under the system temporary directory (`proofline-check/<unique-id>`).
Retain that directory if evidence must survive temporary-file cleanup.
The original request bytes, selected file manifest, candidate identity and exact
command arrays are bound to the report and separate host evidence. `status`
detects changed or missing frozen inputs and evidence. Later live-source edits
do not change the old frozen candidate; checking new work requires a new run.

For optional managed coding, use `run` with the same arguments plus
`--stage-seconds 600`. It still requires a clean source repository. The total
`--seconds` budget counts capture, boundary preflight and command execution;
`--check-seconds` caps each selected command. A timeout or unavailable tool
produces unavailable evidence, while an executed nonzero command produces a
failure. No checks run until the native boundary canaries pass.

Checks run against a **frozen, read-only candidate** under native protection,
without network access or writes to product files. No dependency installation
takes place; checks requiring in-tree writes need a different observation path.
A bounded report records exact argv, native execution receipts, usage when
available, a candidate identity, and distinct `CHECKS PASSED`,
`CHECKS FAILED`, `CHECKS UNAVAILABLE`, `EXECUTION UNAVAILABLE` and
`STALE CHECKS` observations. `status` detects candidate/source/check drift
after an apparent success. Partial or unavailable implementation handoffs do
not become successful check claims.

**User journey:** An existing coding agent implements a CLI option, supplies
the complete original request plus selected CLI and regression checks, and
calls `check`. Proofline freezes that work and returns command evidence without
launching another model. The same agent owns any fixes and the final handoff,
including requirements not demonstrated by the selected checks.

The supported runtime keeps separate small modules for CLI, Git snapshots
(`checks/candidate_snapshot.py`), one coding attempt, native checks,
and exact receipt readback. Historical host diagnostics remain available
for offline security testing, not as an extra acceptance stage. Successful
Linux CI does **not** establish a qualified live macOS/Codex boundary.

## Agent-first scope

The existing agent owns planning, implementation, self-tests and repairs;
Proofline owns frozen identities, bounded checks, receipts and truthful
feedback. Direct tasks require neither P2P nor Intentline. Already-authorized
contracts may inform later optional evidence mapping without replanning or
silently narrowing the original request. Local checking never authorizes push,
PR, merge or deployment. New mandatory stages must earn their latency and
blocking risk through improved *independently correct deliveries*.

See [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) for the small product contract and
# Proofline vNext — lean implementation plan

The supported `check`/`run`/`status` workflow is the product baseline.
The [design](DESIGN.md) is agent-first; S0–S6's previous mandatory
review/proof/certification architecture was abandoned. Historical source
and reports are [pinned in Git](docs/RESEARCH-ARCHIVE.md), not imported
by the current CLI.

## Minimal active architecture

- `proofline.py`: small public `check`/`run`/`status` CLI. It keeps minimal
  compatibility exports for already recorded native study tools.
- `checks/candidate_snapshot.py`: exact clean-source Git snapshot or current tracked/non-ignored
  working-file snapshot, path validation and frozen candidate identity, without agent/review policy.
- `checks/local_run.py`: bounded episode orchestration and exact status
  revalidation, retaining distinct check failure/unavailability/staleness.
- `checks/coding_attempt.py`: one autonomous Codex implementation dispatch per turn,
  optionally persisting/resuming the same implementer for one correction,
  without an independent reviewer/prover or a second acceptance verdict.
- `checks/native_checks.py`: trusted host command receipts and protected
  check execution.
- `checks/feedback.py`: deterministic, optional caller-grounded failure
  annotations and concise check-scoped reports, with separately hash-bound
  bounded process receipts. No model inference or semantic certification.
- `checks/promise_evidence.py`: optional exact-source S1/R-id mapping and
  deterministic link-to-receipt reporting, including self-reported gaps and
  explicit coverage UNKNOWN. No additional model, source rewriting or peer.
- `checks/intentline_advisory.py`: optional **data-only** reader for completed
  single-S1 initial Intentline JSON exports, with exact source, file, contract
  and revision digests, preserved advisory constraints/gaps, explicit argv links
  and frozen local readback. No producer import, lineage flattening or approval.
- `checks/host_probe.py` and `checks/codex_live.py`: existing qualified
  sandbox, process lifecycle and model transport protections. S0 diagnostic
  helpers remain available for offline regressions, but are not called as
  extra acceptance stages by the supported runner.
- `tests/test_check_only.py`, `tests/test_local_run.py`, `tests/test_supported_cli.py`,
  `tests/test_host_probe.py`, `tests/test_codex_live.py`, and retained
  native S0 fixture controls: the supported runner and its boundary
  regressions.

No old delivery/recovery/publisher runtime, source-contract certifier,
historical native Intentline `deliver` controller, S3–S6 corpus generator,
or benchmark coordinator is imported by the supported runner. The optional
JSON advisory adapter does not execute peers or grant authority.

## Small issue-ordered next steps

1. [#9 — Baseline](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/9):
   define a fixed, independently evaluated comparison, including genuine
   alternatives, defects, failure/no-handoff denominators and resource use.
   Keep the original S6 benchmark only as historical reference.
2. [#10 — Core extraction](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/10):
   finish simplifying native helper boundaries without breaking validated
   sandbox and receipt controls. This cleanup is significant groundwork.
3. [#11 — Check-only](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/11), implemented:
   existing coding agents obtain frozen checks with zero new model calls,
   safely handling dirty/untracked work without mutation. Original request,
   selected manifest, exact argv and host evidence are bound to each record.
4. [#12 — Invocation](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/12),

   reduce setup and show concise, actionable native observations while keeping
   raw bounded host receipts and optional expected/observed annotations separate.
   Source-linked R IDs are advisory even when optional #13 command links exist.
5. [#13 — Promise/evidence](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/13):
   implemented as optional check-only source-linked rows, receipt-bound status,
   untested clauses and unverified gap proposals, never certification.
   [#23](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/23) adds a separate
   **opt-in** reader of completed initial Intentline JSON exports and their
   unverified promises/gaps; no mandatory installation or adoption.
6. [#15 — Correction](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/15), implemented:
   opt-in `run --correct-once` resumes the bound implementer after an intact
   Python assertion failure. Both candidates and their receipts remain bound;
   all selected checks rerun under one cumulative budget. No extra dispatch

# Proofline

**A small, optional helper to autonomous coding agents.** Proofline preserves
an original request, freezes an existing working candidate, and executes
caller-selected checks without another model dispatch. It also offers one
optional bounded coding attempt. Passing commands are evidence
**only about those commands**, not proof of every requirement.

## Skill name and installation

The canonical agent skill is [`skills/proofline-check/SKILL.md`](skills/proofline-check/SKILL.md), named `proofline-check`. The root [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md) remains as a migration pointer; the former explicit skill name `proofline` is retired. This renames only the skill: continue using `proofline.py check`, `proofline.py run`, and `proofline.py status`.

Install the package directory as a symlink so it remains one canonical set of
instructions. In the repository, links in the skill resolve relative to its
`skills/proofline-check/` location. Codex supports personal
`~/.agents/skills/` and repository `.agents/skills/` locations; Claude Code
supports personal `~/.claude/skills/` and repository `.claude/skills/`
locations. For a personal install, replace `/absolute/path/to/proofline` with
this checkout's path:

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.agents/skills"
ln -s /absolute/path/to/proofline/skills/proofline-check "$HOME/.agents/skills/proofline-check"

mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude/skills"
ln -s /absolute/path/to/proofline/skills/proofline-check "$HOME/.claude/skills/proofline-check"
```

For repository-local installation from the repository root, use the relevant
host location:

```sh
mkdir -p .agents/skills
ln -s ../../skills/proofline-check .agents/skills/proofline-check

# Or for Claude Code
mkdir -p .claude/skills
ln -s ../../skills/proofline-check .claude/skills/proofline-check
```

An installed skill can be discovered automatically by its host, but discovery
does not guarantee that the host will invoke it for a given task. Request
`proofline-check` explicitly when needed. The skill remains optional; direct
CLI use does not require skill installation or discovery. Installing it adds no
mandatory planning, reviewer, prover, authorization, or model-dispatch stage.

## Quick start — let the existing agent check its work

No planning step, acceptance-contract file, or test-configuration file is needed.
After implementing a change, the **same coding agent** chooses relevant,
already-available project checks and calls Proofline directly:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py check \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/product \
  --request 'Reject blank usernames while preserving Unicode and CLI compatibility.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B cli.py --version'
```

This is an example: choose commands and public interfaces that actually exist
in the target repository. `check` captures the working tree (including ordinary
uncommitted changes), runs exactly those checks and **dispatches zero coding
models**. Its returned report names the frozen candidate and any failed or
unavailable checks, not an automatic assertion that every request was fulfilled.

For a bounded **optional managed coding attempt**, use the same direct inputs:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B proofline.py run \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/clean-product \
  --request 'Add a --version flag without changing existing CLI behavior.' \
  --command '/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -B -m unittest discover -s tests' \
  --stage-seconds 600
```

Rename Proofline agent skill to proofline-check

## Why
Intentline's existing skills use the `<project>-<action>` convention (`intentline-plan`, `intentline-audit`, `intentline-slice`), while Proofline's single skill currently declares `name: proofline` in its root `SKILL.md`. Renaming that skill to **`proofline-check`** makes its purpose clearer and makes explicit invocation consistent across the two projects.

## Scope
Rename **the skill**, not the Proofline project, Python package, or CLI. Keep **one** Proofline skill covering check-only verification, evidence/feedback, optional Intentline input, and optional managed `run`. Prioritize agent-friendly discoverability, correct installation guidance, and minimal change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Change the canonical skill's frontmatter to `name: proofline-check` with a concise trigger-focused description: use after an existing coding agent implements a change to execute selected tests against the frozen candidate and report actual failures / missing evidence; mention that it is optional and model-free in `check` mode.
- [ ] Determine and document the supported skill installation/discovery path for at least Codex and Claude Code. If a standard `skills/proofline-check/SKILL.md` directory is needed, provide it without silently breaking the existing root `SKILL.md` entry or creating two independently maintained divergent instructions. Preserve relative documentation/code links under the chosen layout.
- [ ] Update README, skill instructions, examples, and any current references that invoke or install the skill under its old name. Distinguish **automatic discovery when installed** from guaranteed automatic invocation (not guaranteed).
- [ ] Preserve the existing `proofline.py check`, `run`, and `status` commands, direct/file source inputs, optional Intentline integration, zero-extra-model check-only behavior, receipt integrity, and safety boundaries. Do **not** rename the CLI to `proofline-check`.
- [ ] Test/validate skill metadata, single canonical definition or explicit compatibility alias (if needed), relative link resolution, supported install packaging, and documentation consistency. If an old explicit skill invocation is no longer supported, document the migration clearly rather than claiming unverified compatibility.
- [ ] Confirm no new mandatory planning, reviewer/prover, authorization, or model-dispatch stage was introduced.

## Out of scope
Splitting Proofline into multiple skills merely for symmetry, changing Intentline skill names, merging repositories, altering check execution semantics, or making skill discovery mandatory for direct CLI use.

## Notes
Current skill: [root SKILL.md](https://github.com/grove/proofline/blob/main/SKILL.md). Intentline comparison: [intentline-plan](https://github.com/grove/intentline/blob/main/skills/intentline-plan/SKILL.md). This is a naming/documentation/discoverability improvement, **not** an independently demonstrated correctness improvement.
